text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's interim cabinet may reach a preliminary funding agreement with the International Monetary Fund and receive the first tranche by end-March or beginning of April, Finance Minister Svetoslav Gavriiski said after a meeting with the visiting IMF mission. @
-- Bulgaria's caretaker government will seek to reschedule debt payments due to the Paris Club of official creditors this year, said Gavriiski.
-- Bulgaria's President Petar Stoyanov left for a five-day trip to Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary, where he is expected to reaffirm his country's desire to join the European Union and NATO.

-- Bulgaria's caretaker Prime Minister Stefan Sofianski is leaving on Thursday on a two-day visit to the neighbouring former Yugoslav republic of Macedonia, where he is expected to meet his counterpart Branko Crvenkovski.

-- Bulgaria's former Socialist Prime Minister Zhan Videnov was personally responsible for the current severe wheat shortage because he had exercised proper control over grain exports, interim Interior Minister Bogomil Bonev said. @
-- Bulgaria's caretaker cabinet is to discuss today a draft for a two-fold rise of electricity, central heating and coal prices from March 1.
-- Bulgaria was officially included among the candidates a full NATO membership from the former East Bloc, Bulgaria's interim foreign minister Stoyan Stalev said upon return from a visit to Brussels.
